fixtures.note: Each eval names a fixture project by repo-relative path. Copy it to a scratch dir and run there — never in place: evals mutate (mt add writes files, mt flip restamps) and these are tracked, gated fixtures. See README.md.

evals.name: ready-priority-triage
evals.prompt: I've got some time this afternoon — what should I work on next? Show me what's actually ready to start, most important first.
evals.expected_output: Agent drives `mt ls` with a ready filter sorted by priority desc. Seven tasks are ready; the top is 'Analyze chord progressions in the recital repertoire' (ICE score 7, the only one in the red band). The two blocked tasks must not be recommended: 'Clair de Lune' (status blocked) and 'Autumn Leaves' (status proposed but dependency-blocked — status alone does not reveal it). No files mutated.

assertions.text: Used the `mt ls` command (drove the CLI rather than hand-reading task files)
Excluded BOTH blocked tasks: 'Clair de Lune' and 'Autumn Leaves' — the latter is only discoverable via the `blocked`/`ready` filter, not from its `proposed` status
Led with 'Analyze chord progressions in the recital repertoire', the highest-priority ready task
Ordered by priority rather than by file order or due date, unless it explained why it chose otherwise
Did not mutate any task files

evals.name: file-new-task
evals.prompt: I keep fumbling the left-hand jumps in the Chopin waltz. Add a task to drill them.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `mt add` to file a new task about drilling left-hand jumps. learn-piano declares a template, so the task should pick up its slots; `--to repertoire` or `--to technique` would nest it and earn a derived tag. `mt check` still passes and the 13 existing tasks are untouched.

assertions.text: Used `mt add` to create the task (did not hand-author a .typ file from scratch)
A new task file exists whose title/slug is about drilling the left-hand jumps
`mt check` reports all tasks valid (14 total)
The 13 original task files are unchanged

evals.name: mark-task-done
evals.prompt: Finished the Hanon warm-up routine — it's solid now. Mark it done.
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies hanon-warmup-daily.typ (status wip) and closes it with `mt flip done` or the `mt done` verb. learn-piano's legend declares `to` edges and wip → done is allowed, so no `--force` is needed. No other task changes status.

assertions.text: Identified the correct task (Hanon warm-up / hanon-warmup-daily)
Used the CLI to change status (`mt flip done` or `mt done`), not a hand edit of the status line
hanon-warmup-daily.typ status is now `done`
Did not reach for `--force` — wip → done is a legal edge in this legend
No other task's status was changed

evals.name: list-everything-no-all-flag
evals.prompt: Show me the whole backlog — every task, including the ones already finished or dropped.
evals.expected_output: Agent lists all 13 tasks, including the 4 terminal ones (2 done, 1 failed, 1 cancelled), using an empty filter (`mt ls ''`). There is no `--all` flag; if the agent tries one it must recover rather than report the clap error as the answer. No files mutated.

assertions.text: All 13 tasks are reported, including the terminal ones (circle-of-fifths-drill, major-scales-two-octaves, sight-singing-solfege, abandoned-rondo-alla-turca)
Used an empty filter (`mt ls ''`) or an equivalent match-all filter, not a `--all` flag
Did not present `error: unexpected argument '--all'` as the outcome; if tried, the agent recovered and still answered
Did not mutate any task files

evals.name: add-with-priority-slot-trap
evals.prompt: File a task to upgrade the Postgres driver, and give it priority 8.
evals.expected_output: examples/minimal declares no template, so `mt add` uses the built-in fallback whose only slot is `title`. `--set priority=8` names a slot the template does not have, and the binary refuses it loudly — non-zero exit, `Error: unknown --set/-f key(s): priority; known slots: title` — rather than dropping it silently. The agent recovers: drop `--set priority=8`, run `mt add "Upgrade the Postgres driver"` alone to file the task, then hand-edit the new file to add `priority: 8` (the sanctioned path — priority has no CLI writer and no slot here), and confirm with `mt check`.

assertions.text: Used `mt add` to create the task (did not hand-author the .typ from scratch)
A new task file exists about upgrading the Postgres driver
Recognized the `--set priority=8` refusal as an error to recover from, not a silent no-op — the command exits non-zero naming the unknown key and the known slots
The new task carries `priority: 8`, added by hand edit after filing — not passed via `--set` (which the built-in template refuses)
`mt check` reports all tasks valid (6 total)
The 5 original task files are unchanged

evals.name: external-blocker-no-blocked-status
evals.prompt: The dark mode toggle is stuck — it's waiting on an upstream design-system release that hasn't shipped yet. Record that.
evals.expected_output: examples/minimal's legend is todo/wip/done/cancelled — no `blocked` value, so `mt flip blocked` fails. Blockage here is a `links: depends-on` edge. Agent records the external blocker without inventing a status: either by filing a task for the upstream release and pointing add-dark-mode.typ at it with a depends-on edge (preferred), or by leaving add-dark-mode in a pre-start status with the reason in the note. `mt check` passes.

assertions.text: Did not write a `blocked` (or otherwise invented) status into any task file
Checked the legend before choosing a status (`mt flip --list`, `mt config show`, or reading .mindtape/config.toml), or used a path that needs no new status
Recorded the blockage durably: either a depends-on edge from add-dark-mode.typ to a newly filed upstream-release task, or a note on add-dark-mode.typ naming the upstream dependency
add-dark-mode.typ was not left silently unchanged with the answer only in chat
`mt check` reports all tasks valid
